messages.subject: Tumor evolution using SNAs
parts:
Hi Jiang,

If there is only SNAs pesent in our sample as given in example'toy3', so what will be the probable input. The dataset file (toy3.rda) contains 'R, X, realZ, realP, realVAF, Mu, Tau, sna_cluster'. I am very confused over this, I just have R, X and VAFs for my dataset.

I've read 'How do I generate SNA input for Canopy?' on GitHub page but getting no clue how can I run this using just  R, X and VAFs? Do I need any other information as well?

Thanks!

Best wishes,

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Tumor evolution using SNAs
parts:
Thanks for your interest in Canopy! Yes you only need R and X (R/X is your observed VAF, i.e., what you also have) to infer phylogeny using SNAs only. 

realZ, realP, realVAF are the real quantities that we simulate R and X from, which is used as a gold standard.

Mu, Tau, sna_cluster is from pre-clustering step, which is optional but is recommended if you have many SNAs and they form clusters by visual check. See here https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/tree/master/clustering for more details.

If you have Mu, Tau, sna_cluster, use canopy.sample.cluster.nocna; if you don’t perform pre-clustering, use canopy.sample.nocna. More details can be found here https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy/blob/master/instruction/sampling_mode.md.

Hope that this clarifies. A side note is that if you are using only SNAs as input, you should exclude all SNAs with VAF > 50% since they have to be within CNA regions, which you don’t have input of. Also from our experience multiple tree configurations can be possible especially if only SNAs are used as input, thus you should definitely increase the number of chains in the sampling steps so that as much tree space as possible is sampled.

Hope that this clarifies and let me know if you have further questions.

Yuchao
